device.name: Dyson Air Purifier
device.notes:
Dyson connected purifiers advertise a local MQTT broker on port 1883 via mDNS. The device is the broker. Local credentials are derived from the device serial and WiFi password during/after pairing. Known topics are scoped by product type and serial — {productType}/{serial}/status/current and {productType}/{serial}/command — and local control does not require internet access after pairing.
Note (2026-07): the original shenxn/libdyson and ha-dyson projects are stale; the maintained continuation is libdyson-wg/libdyson-neon (PyPI libdyson-neon), and Home Assistant core removed its built-in Dyson integration in 2024.1.

issued_to_client: Local MQTT username — the device serial number
Local MQTT password — base64 of the SHA-512 digest of the sticker WiFi password
credentials.notes: The MQTT password derivation is the published libdyson/ha-dyson behaviour: hash the sticker password with SHA-512 and base64-encode the raw digest. Because it is derived from a printed static secret, anyone who photographs the sticker keeps local control forever — including after a resale.

factory_reset.effect: Clears the stored WiFi credentials and returns the machine to hosting its setup AP. The sticker credentials are hardware identity and do not change.

procedures.indicator: The display flashes to confirm the WiFi reset.
procedures.name: Standby button held

steps.action: With the machine powered on, press and hold the standby button on the unit (not the remote) until the display flashes.
steps.notes: Hold time varies by model; verify against the model's manual.

methods.description: The machine hosts its own WPA-protected access point whose SSID and passphrase are printed on the device sticker. The app joins that AP and hands over the home network credentials.

softap.passphrase_source: Printed on the device sticker and on the spare label supplied in the box.

steps.action: Read the product SSID and WiFi password from the sticker on the machine.
Send the home network credentials to the machine.
steps.notes: Exact request layout not captured in this project; the vendor app performs this step today.

steps.action: Rejoin the home network and confirm the machine advertises _dyson_mqtt._tcp.local.

setup.notes: Dyson machines are one of the few devices here whose local credentials are printed on the hardware rather than issued by a server. That makes them fully recoverable without the vendor cloud — but it also means the sticker (and the spare label in the box) is the only copy of the secret. Photograph it before mounting the machine somewhere awkward.

rejoin.notes: Re-provisioning goes back through the setup AP, so a router change means resetting the machine's WiFi and repeating onboarding. The local MQTT credentials are unaffected because they are derived from the sticker, not from the network.

characteristics: Air purifier and fan with local MQTT broker.
variants.name: Dyson Pure Cool

characteristics: Air purifier, heater, and fan with local MQTT broker (product type 455).

PREFIX CONFLICT: a 2018 capture shows PE6 with product type 455 (Pure Hot+Cool Link), while this project's own live probe below saw a PE6 unit as a Humidify+Cool. The prefix may be reused across product lines — identify by the MQTT product type, not the serial prefix alone.
variants.name: Dyson Pure Hot+Cool Link

mqtt_topics.description: State reports including fan mode, oscillation, air quality, filter state, temperature, humidity, and device mode. Example: 438/F3H-US-PFA5664A/status/current.
mqtt_topics.name: Current Status

mqtt_topics.description: UNVERIFIED: this topic appears in no known implementation (libdyson, libdyson-neon, libpurecool, Hubitat drivers, matterbridge-dyson-robot). Availability is normally inferred from the broker connection, not a device topic. Retained for provenance; do not rely on it.
mqtt_topics.name: Connection Status

mqtt_topics.description: Command topic for mode, power, fan speed, oscillation, auto mode, and humidifier controls.
mqtt_topics.name: Command
